in_hebrew.name: יעקב
in_hebrew.meaning: מְקַלְקֶל שֶׁל הַיָּם וּמְגוּרָם שֶׁל הַיָּם
in_hebrew.long_meaning: יעקב - (Yaaqov) - (Strong's 3290) - Name of Jacob - son of Isaac, grandson of Abraham - meaning: supplanter - or one who takes the place of another - in biblical context: Jacob was the son of Isaac who supplanted his twin brother Esau and took his birthright, representing the struggle between faith and doubt - historically in Hebrew tradition: Jacob is considered a symbol of the Jewish people and their relationship with God - spiritually: Jacob's name reflects the idea of struggle and perseverance in the face of adversity, reminding us that we can overcome our own personal struggles and doubts - in Christian tradition: Jacob's story is seen as a type of Christ, where Jacob represents the chosen people and Christ represents the ultimate savior

in_greek.name: Ἰαχίνθης
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἰαχίνθης - (Iachinthēs) - Origin: Hebrew name Ya'aqov - meaning: radiant and faultless - in biblical context: the name Iachinthēs appears in the New Testament as a reference to the stone given to the high priest by the soldiers during the crucifixion of Jesus - historically in early Christian tradition: the name Iachinthēs symbolizes the idea of purity and innocence, highlighting the contrast between the righteous and the unrighteous - spiritually: the name Iachinthēs reminds us that we should strive to be free from sin and to live a life that reflects the character of Christ - in modern Christian usage: the name Iachinthēs is often associated with virtues such as honesty, integrity, and compassion

in_latin.name: Iachinthes
in_latin.long_meaning: Iachinthes - Origin Hebrew name Ya'aqov - meaning: radiant and faultless - in early Christian tradition the name Iachinthes was used to signify the virtues of purity and innocence, highlighting the contrast between the righteous and the unrighteous - historically in Christian tradition: the name Iachinthes represents the idea of living a life free from sin and striving to reflect the character of Christ - spiritually: the name Iachinthes reminds us to strive for purity and to live a life that honors God
